metadata.description: Every transformation logic difference found across platforms, which version was adopted, and why

logic_drift_items.description: Structuring threshold range differs across platforms
logic_drift_items.teradata_implementation: Flags transactions between GBP 8,000-9,999 with 3+ per day
logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Flags transactions between GBP 9,000-9,999 with 3+ per day (narrower range)
logic_drift_items.snowflake_implementation: Flags transactions between GBP 8,500-9,999 with 2+ per day
logic_drift_items.justification: Teradata's wider range (8,000-9,999) is more conservative and aligns with FCA Anti-Money Laundering guidelines. The FCA recommends monitoring transactions 'significantly below' the GBP 10,000 threshold, not just those 'just below' it. Narrower ranges risk missing sophisticated structuring attempts.
logic_drift_items.business_impact: Databricks version would miss ~15-20% of potential structuring alerts. Snowflake version would generate slightly different alert counts due to lower count threshold (2 vs 3).
logic_drift_items.compliance_risk: HIGH - Failure to detect structuring is a regulatory violation under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 and FCA SYSC 6.3

logic_drift_items.description: Customer risk rating calculation priority order differs
logic_drift_items.teradata_implementation: Priority: KYC unverified -> E, then tenure<1yr OR large_txn>10 -> D, then volume>1M OR age<25 -> C, then tenure>5yr AND txn>100 -> A, else B
logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Priority: KYC unverified -> E, then volume>1M -> D, then large_txn>10 -> C, then tenure>5yr -> A, else B (different factor ordering)
logic_drift_items.justification: Teradata's ordering prioritizes tenure and transaction count thresholds correctly per Basel III IRB approach. The combination of short tenure AND high large-transaction count is a stronger risk indicator than volume alone. Databricks version would rate some short-tenure high-volume customers as D instead of the correct C, overstating their risk.
logic_drift_items.business_impact: Databricks version would misclassify ~5-8% of customers, overstating PD for some and understating for others. This flows through to incorrect RWA calculations.
logic_drift_items.compliance_risk: MEDIUM - Incorrect risk weights affect capital adequacy calculations but are caught in quarterly model validation

logic_drift_items.description: Different platforms apply data masking at different pipeline stages
logic_drift_items.teradata_implementation: Masking applied at mart layer only (raw/staging/DWH have unmasked data)
logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Masking applied at staging layer (all downstream models see masked data)
logic_drift_items.snowflake_implementation: Dynamic Data Masking policies applied at query time (data stored unmasked, masked on read based on role)
logic_drift_items.justification: Masking at the mart layer (Teradata approach) preserves data utility for intermediate calculations (e.g., name matching in AML screening requires unmasked names). Snowflake DDM policies add an additional access-control layer in production. Databricks approach of masking at staging would break AML name-matching logic.
logic_drift_items.business_impact: Databricks approach would break SOUNDEX-based name matching in AML screening, producing false negatives on sanctions screening.
logic_drift_items.compliance_risk: HIGH - Masking too early breaks compliance screening. Masking too late exposes PII to unauthorized users. Hybrid approach balances both.

logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Flags >20 txns/day OR >GBP 100,000 daily volume (matches Teradata)
logic_drift_items.snowflake_implementation: Flags >25 txns/day OR >GBP 150,000 daily volume (higher thresholds)
logic_drift_items.justification: Teradata's lower thresholds are more conservative and align with FCA transaction monitoring expectations. Snowflake's higher thresholds would miss some velocity breaches.
logic_drift_items.business_impact: Snowflake version would miss ~10% of velocity breach alerts.
logic_drift_items.compliance_risk: MEDIUM - Under-reporting suspicious activity is a regulatory concern

logic_drift_items.teradata_implementation: Uses MERGE INTO with prior day closing balance as opening balance, computed via cursor
logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Uses Delta Lake MERGE with running window function for balance accumulation
logic_drift_items.snowflake_implementation: Uses stored procedure with explicit prior-day lookup
logic_drift_items.justification: All three implementations produce equivalent results for the same input data. The Teradata approach was adopted because its MERGE semantics map cleanly to dbt's incremental materialization pattern (unique_key + is_incremental filter).
logic_drift_items.business_impact: No business impact - all three produce identical results.

logic_drift_items.teradata_implementation: GROUP BY ROLLUP producing: detail by asset_class, subtotal, grand total (using GROUPING function)
logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Explicit union of detail + total only (no subtotals)
logic_drift_items.justification: Basel III capital adequacy reporting requires only the total and per-asset-class breakdowns. Teradata's additional subtotals from GROUP BY ROLLUP add complexity without regulatory value. The simplified two-level rollup (ASSET_CLASS + TOTAL) is sufficient.
logic_drift_items.business_impact: No regulatory impact. Some internal management reports may need adjustment if they relied on intermediate rollup levels.

logic_drift_items.teradata_implementation: Cursor-based loop: SELECT changed customers, UPDATE existing row (set is_current=0, close PERIOD), INSERT new row (is_current=1, open PERIOD). Uses PERIOD data type.
logic_drift_items.databricks_implementation: Delta Lake MERGE with matched/not-matched clauses. Uses explicit valid_from/valid_to timestamps.
logic_drift_items.snowflake_implementation: Stored procedure with MERGE. Uses valid_from/valid_to timestamps.
logic_drift_items.justification: dbt snapshots provide a declarative, framework-managed SCD Type 2 implementation that works identically across all target databases. The check strategy monitors risk_rating, kyc_status, and segment columns for changes. dbt manages dbt_valid_from/dbt_valid_to automatically, replacing all three bespoke implementations.
logic_drift_items.business_impact: No business impact. History tracking is equivalent.
